- `text` is valid UTF-8 of at most 100,000 lines and 1,000,000 bytes; a file given to `load_config` is at most 1,000,000 bytes.
- No case folding and no Unicode normalization of keys or values.
- Keep `Config`, `ConfigError` and `LoadError` with their variants and derives exactly as given.
- Chapters 1–9 only: no `unwrap()`, no closures or closure-taking methods, no trait implementations, generics or lifetimes of your own.
hints: Keep each setting in an `Option` (`let mut port: Option<u16> = None;`) while you read, and build the `Config` only after the loop: that is what guarantees no partial result escapes.

`let mut pieces = line.split('=');` gives the key with `pieces.next().ok_or(ConfigError::BadLine(n))?`, the value the same way, and a third `pieces.next()` that is `Some` means a second `=`. A numeric value converts with `value.parse::<u16>().ok().ok_or(…)?`, and the range check comes after it.

Decide the key with one `match key { "host" => …, "port" => …, "workers" => …, _ => return Err(ConfigError::UnknownKey(n, key.to_string())) }`, checking `is_some()` for the duplicate before looking at the value. At the end, `host.ok_or(ConfigError::Missing("host".to_string()))?` comes before the same line for `port`, and `workers.unwrap_or(4)` supplies the default. In `load_config`, `match std::fs::read_to_string(path) { Ok(text) => text, Err(error) => return Err(LoadError::Io(error.kind())) }`.
problems.solution_approach_md: `parse_config` keeps three `Option`s and a line counter that goes up for every line. After trimming, blank and `#` lines are skipped. `split('=')` must give exactly two pieces, taken with `next().ok_or(BadLine)?`. A `match` on the trimmed key returns `UnknownKey` for anything else and otherwise reports whether the key was already set, which gives `Duplicate`. The value is then checked for its key: non-empty for `host`, `parse::<u16>` and non-zero for `port`, `parse::<u8>` and 1–64 for `workers`, each failure being `InvalidValue` with the line number. After the loop, `ok_or(Missing(…))?` on `host` and then `port` and `unwrap_or(4)` on `workers` build the `Config`. `load_config` matches the result of `read_to_string`, turning an error into `Io(error.kind())`, and matches the parse result to wrap its error in `Parse`.
problems.idiomatic_md: Each error variant carries exactly what a person needs to fix the file, a line number and a key, and returning at the first error keeps every later check simple because it can assume the earlier ones passed. `LoadError` keeps the two layers apart: the caller can tell "could not read the file" from "the file says something wrong" by matching one enum, and an I/O error is classified by its `ErrorKind`, which is the same on every system, rather than by its message text.

problems.title: Proper errors
problems.description_md:
Until now the catalogue said "no" with `false` or `None`, and the caller could not tell an unknown book from a member at the limit. LM9 gives every failure a name: a `LibraryError` value that carries the id or text involved (Book ch. 9.2, "Recoverable Errors with `Result`"). It also adds a small command language, a parser that turns one line of text into a `Command`, and `Library::execute`, which runs a command and returns the text to show. Runtime rows run in a harness whose crate root is the learner's `src/lib.rs`, so they name the root re-exports directly (`Library`, `LibraryError`, `Command`, `parse_command`, `Book`, `Status`, `Member`).

**Part 1 · The error type and `add_member`**

The starter is the accepted LM8 reference solution with these additions only: a new file `src/error.rs` holding `LibraryError` with its seven variants (`NoSuchBook(u32)`, `NoSuchMember(u32)`, `NotAvailable(u32)`, `LimitReached(u32)`, `NotBorrowed(u32)`, `DuplicateMember(u32)` and `BadCommand(String)`); a new file `src/command.rs` holding `Command` with its five variants and placeholder bodies for `parse_command` and `Library::execute`; `src/lib.rs` declaring `pub mod command;` and `pub mod error;` and re-exporting `pub use command::{Command, parse_command};` and `pub use error::LibraryError;`; and, in `src/library.rs`, `use crate::error::LibraryError` and the new signatures of the three methods that change, with placeholder bodies. Both new enums derive `Debug`, `Clone` and `PartialEq`, so tests can print and compare them.

`add_member(id, name, premium)` now returns `Result<(), LibraryError>`: `Ok(())` after inserting `Member::new(id, name, premium)`, or `Err(LibraryError::DuplicateMember(id))` when the id is taken, leaving the existing member (and any loans it has) unchanged.

Everything else stays exactly as LM8 left it: `fees.rs`, `text.rs`, `book.rs`, `member.rs` and the menu in `src/main.rs` are unchanged, `add_book`, `book`, `member`, `books_by`, `search_titles`, `count_by_status` and `authors` keep their signatures and answers, and the menu is still not connected to the catalogue. The LM6 regression suite and the menu transcripts still pass.

**Part 2 · `checkout` and `return_book`**

`checkout(book_id, member_id, today)` returns `Result<u32, LibraryError>`: `Ok(due day)` on success. It checks, in this order, and returns the first failure without changing anything:

1. no book has `book_id`: `Err(NoSuchBook(book_id))`;
2. no member has `member_id`: `Err(NoSuchMember(member_id))`;
3. the book is not `Available` (borrowed, or lost): `Err(NotAvailable(book_id))`;
4. the member already has their limit of loans (3, or 6 for premium): `Err(LimitReached(member_id))`;
5. `today` is greater than `u32::MAX - 28` (4294967267), the last day whose premium due day fits in a `u32`: `Err(BadCommand(format!("checkout {book_id} {member_id} {today}")))`, the canonical command text.

Then it hands the stored book and member to `Book::checkout`, as LM8 did, and returns the due day, `today + 14` or `today + 28`.

`return_book(book_id, today)` returns `Result<u32, LibraryError>`: `Ok(fee in cents)` on success. It checks, in order: no such book gives `Err(NoSuchBook(book_id))`; a book that is not borrowed (available, or lost) gives `Err(NotBorrowed(book_id))`; and if the borrower recorded in the book is not a member, `Err(NoSuchMember(borrower id))`. Otherwise it returns `Book::return_to_shelf`'s fee: the LM3 late fee, with the book available again and the member's count reduced. Return days may be any `u32`. The public API cannot make a book `Lost` or remove a member, so the "lost" and "missing borrower" cases are stated for completeness but no row can reach them.

**Part 3 · `parse_command`**

`parse_command(line)` turns one line into a `Command`. Every rejection is `Err(LibraryError::BadCommand(line.to_string()))`, carrying the original `line` exactly as given, surrounding whitespace included.

1. Trim `line` with `trim`. If the trimmed text still contains a line feed or a carriage return, it is two lines joined together: reject it. (A final LF or CRLF is outer whitespace and is harmless.)
2. The keyword is the first word of the trimmed text (`split_whitespace`); an empty or blank line is rejected. Keywords are exact and lower-case: `ADD`, `Find` or `remove` are rejected, and so is a word with the keyword glued to more text, such as `add|A|B|1`.
3. `add <title>|<author>|<year>`: the rest of the line after the keyword is split at `|` into exactly three fields, each trimmed. Title and author may be empty and keep their inner spacing (`Book::new` normalizes later); the year must parse as a `u16`. Gives `Command::Add { title, author, year }`.
4. `checkout <book> <member> <day>`: exactly three more words, each a `u32`, and the day at most 4294967267. Gives `Command::Checkout { book_id, member_id, today }`.
5. `return <book> <day>`: exactly two more words, each a `u32` (any day). Gives `Command::Return { book_id, today }`.
6. `find <query>`: the rest of the trimmed line after the keyword and the whitespace that follows it, which must not be empty; inner spacing is kept. Gives `Command::Find(query)`.
7. `report`: no more words. Gives `Command::Report`.

Numbers follow Rust's unsigned parsing: ASCII digits with an optional leading `+`, leading zeros allowed, no sign `-`, no full-width digits. Words are separated by any whitespace, including tabs and U+3000.

**Part 4 · `Library::execute`**

`execute(cmd)` consumes a `Command` and returns `Result<String, LibraryError>`; the text has no final newline:

- `Add` calls `add_book` and gives `Added book {id}.`
- `Checkout` calls `checkout` and gives `Book {book_id} due on day {due}.`
- `Return` calls `return_book` and gives `Fee: {format_cents(fee)}.`, for example `Fee: $2.25.`
- `Find` calls `search_titles` and gives `Found: ` followed by the ids joined with `, ` and a final `.`, or `Found: none.` when nothing matches.
- `Report` gives `Available: {a}\nBorrowed: {b}\nLost: {l}` from `count_by_status`.

An error from `checkout` or `return_book` is returned unchanged with `?`, and no success text is produced for it. A `Command` built directly is executed as it is, without being reparsed.

```text
Expected: Ok(Command::Add{title:"Rust".to_string(),author:"Ada".to_string(),year:2024})
```

```text
Setup: let mut l=Library::new();
Expression: {l.add_book("X","A",0);let _=l.add_member(7,"M",false);(l.checkout(1,9,0),l.checkout(1,7,10),l.checkout(1,7,10))}
Expected: (Err(LibraryError::NoSuchMember(9)),Ok(24),Err(LibraryError::NotAvailable(1)))
```

```text
Expression: l.execute(Command::Add{title:"The  Rust".to_string(),author:" Ada ".to_string(),year:2024})

```

At most 100,000 `add_book` calls per `Library` and at most 100,000 members; every text argument and command line is valid UTF-8 of at most 100,000 bytes. Member ids use the full `u32` range and years the full `u16` range; `checkout` accepts any `u32` day and refuses days above 4294967267 as Part 2 says. No input may make any function panic. Chapters 1–9 only: no `unwrap()`, no closures or closure-taking methods, no `impl` of `Display`, `Error`, `From` or any other trait, no generics or lifetime annotations of your own, and no new menu options. The package is named `library` (edition 2024, no dependencies) and contains exactly `src/lib.rs`, `src/fees.rs`, `src/text.rs`, `src/book.rs`, `src/member.rs`, `src/library.rs`, `src/error.rs`, `src/command.rs` and `src/main.rs`.
hints: `ok_or` turns a lookup that may be `None` into a `Result` with the error you name: `let i = self.index_of(book_id).ok_or(LibraryError::NoSuchBook(book_id))?;` stops the method with that error when the book is unknown. Check every failure condition before calling `Book::checkout`, so a rejected call cannot have changed anything.

In `parse_command`, trim once, reject an embedded `'\n'` or `'\r'`, and take the keyword with `let mut words = text.split_whitespace();` and `words.next().ok_or(…)?`. The text after the keyword is `text[keyword.len()..].trim_start()`: for `add` split it at `'|'`, for `find` keep it whole. A small helper `fn number(word: Option<&str>, line: &str) -> Result<u32, LibraryError>` that does `word.ok_or(…)?` and `word.parse::<u32>().ok().ok_or(…)` saves repeating the same three lines.

In `execute`, `match cmd { Command::Add { title, author, year } => …, … }` moves each field out of the command. `let due = self.checkout(book_id, member_id, today)?;` returns the error unchanged and continues only on success; for `Find`, push each id with `to_string()` and `", "` between them.
problems.solution_approach_md: `src/lib.rs`, `src/error.rs` and the `Command` enum come complete with the starter. `add_member` checks `contains_key` and returns `DuplicateMember` before inserting. `checkout` gets the book's index and the member with `ok_or(…)?`, then checks availability, the member's limit and the day in the stated order, each with an early `return Err(…)`, and only then calls `Book::checkout` and returns `due_day(today, member.premium)`. `return_book` finds the index, gets the borrower with `borrower().ok_or(NotBorrowed)?` and the member with `ok_or(NoSuchMember)?`, and returns `return_to_shelf`'s fee with `ok_or(NotBorrowed)`. `parse_command` trims, rejects embedded line breaks, splits off the keyword and dispatches on it with `match`; `add` uses a helper that splits at `|` into exactly three trimmed fields and parses the year, and `checkout` and `return` read numbers through a helper that turns a missing or unparsable word into `BadCommand`. `execute` matches the command, calls the library method (with `?` for the two fallible ones) and formats the reply.
problems.idiomatic_md: Replacing `bool` and `Option` with `Result<_, LibraryError>` changes no rule of the library, only what a failure says: the same checks now name the book or member involved, and `?` passes those names straight through `execute` to whoever runs the command. Checking every condition before the first mutation keeps each method all-or-nothing, so an `Err` always means "nothing happened". The parser and the executor are separate on purpose: `parse_command` knows only text and `execute` knows only commands, so either can be tested, or replaced, without the other.
